land.text: the Estonian lands of the former Russian Empire (the page: 'the Estonian Salvation Committee declared the independence of Estonia' on 24 February 1918)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Russian Republic row runs 1917-1919; Soviet Russia gave Estonia up in the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (3 March 1918) and recognised it on 2 February 1920. Reviewer eu-21-a: the russian-republic dossier ends in November 1917, so the counterpart is Soviet Russia (RSFSR), whose ledger loses Estonia to the German Empire in March 1918.

land.text: annexed 'by the Soviet Union as the Estonian SSR' on 6 August 1940

successors.note: Estonia's legal-continuity doctrine (the page: continuity 'was preserved through the government-in-exile') makes the republic of 1991, dossier republic-of-estonia (Cliopatria 'Republic of Estonia' 1992..2024, group eu-22), the same state in law; both rows carry Q191. This dossier follows Cliopatria and the existing ESSR dossier (predecessor estonia, successor republic-of-estonia) and keeps the 1940-1991 interval as its own state.

correction.text: the Estonian lands at the declaration of 24 February 1918

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1919, but Estonia declared independence on 24 February 1918, 'one day before the arrival of German troops to Tallinn'; the Germans secured Narva on 28 February, ran an occupation that did not recognise the Estonian government, and returned power on 19 November 1918. The 1919 outline is drawn for 1918; the occupation pair carries the German years and the war with Soviet Russia (from 28 November 1918) the Narva front.

48,431 km2 against the infobox's 45,335 km2 (no year; ratio 1.07): the interwar state held the strip east of the Narva and Setumaa, which were transferred to the Russian SFSR in 1944 ('the land east of the Narva River and most of Petseri County'). Estonian forces fought beyond this line in 1919 (Valga 31 January, Pskov 25 May, Cesis 23 June, the outskirts of Riga on 3 July), which the shape does not show; the state's own land is as drawn.

48,569 km2 for 1920-1935 (ratio 1.07 to the infobox): the Tartu border of 2 February 1920, which 'corresponded roughly with the position of the front line'; Estonia 'retained a strategic strip to the east of the Narva river and Setumaa in the southeast'. One cell (27.36 E, 59.06 N, Ida-Viru) is added over 1919; no page dates it (digitising difference). The Valga/Valka division with Latvia is not on the pages opened.

48,288 km2 for 1936-1938: three coastal cells of Ida-Viru (27.5-27.7 E, 59.2 N) are gone compared with 1935; no page opened dates a border change then (digitising difference), so the shape stands. Ratio 1.07 to the infobox.

48,288 km2, same cells as 1936-1938. The mutual assistance treaty of 28 September 1939 allowed 'Soviet naval, air and army bases on two Estonian islands and at the port of Paldiski' with 25,000 Soviet soldiers from October 1939; the land stays Estonian until the occupation of June 1940.

correction.text: the 1939 outline for 1940, under Soviet occupation from June

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1939, but the republic lasts until the Soviet annexation of 6 August 1940 (occupation from 16-17 June 1940, 'rigged parliamentary elections' on 14-15 July, the People's Parliament's request of 21 July).

ledger.note: 1918, 24 February: Estonia declares independence. The page: 'the Estonian Salvation Committee declared the independence of Estonia' and formed a provisional government; 'German occupation immediately followed'.

region.text: all of Estonia, from Tallinn (about 25 February) to Narva (28 February)

ledger.note: 1918, February: German troops occupy Estonia. The declaration came 'one day before the arrival of German troops to Tallinn'; the northern force 'secured Narva on 28 February 1918'; 'German occupation authorities refused to recognize the Estonian government'.
1918, 19 November: the Germans hand power back to the Estonian government (the page: they had to 'return power to the Estonian government on 19 November 1918').

region.text: Narva and the east of Estonia, where the Red Army attacked

ledger.note: 1918, 28 November: Soviet Russia invades. 'On 28 November 1918, the Soviet 6th Red Rifle Division attacked the border town of Narva.' The page does not map the Soviet advance; the zone is the researcher's reading (the east, Ida-Viru).

region.text: Narva and the east of Estonia

ledger.note: 1920, 3 January: the ceasefire takes effect ('the peace treaty was concluded on 31 December 1919 and the ceasefire took effect on 3 January 1920'); the Treaty of Tartu follows on 2 February 1920.

region.text: the strip east of the Narva river and Setumaa, kept at Tartu

ledger.note: 1920, 2 February: the Treaty of Tartu fixes the border. 'The Peace Treaty of Tartu was signed by the Republic of Estonia and RSFSR'; 'The agreed frontier corresponded roughly with the position of the front line'; Estonia 'retained a strategic strip to the east of the Narva river and Setumaa in the southeast'. Russia 'renounces voluntarily and forever all sovereign rights' over Estonia (Treaty page, ratified 30 March 1920).

1940, 16 June: the Soviet Union occupies Estonia after the ultimatum of 16 June ('On 16 June 1940 the Soviets issued an ultimatum'); the Estonia page has the Red Army in 'the next day', 17 June, and dates a blockade to 14 June.

1940, 6 August: 'Estonia was annexed by the Soviet Union as the Estonian SSR.' The Baltic page: 'rigged parliamentary elections' on 14-15 July, the People's Parliaments asked to join the Soviet Union on 21 July, and 'in early August the Supreme Soviet of the USSR accepted'.
1940, 6 August: the occupation ends in annexation (the infobox gives the end of the occupation period as 6 August 1940).

1940, 6 August: the republic ends in law and in fact; the West did not recognise the annexation and the government in exile 'was the government recognized by the Western world during the Cold War'. The ESSR dossier dates its nominal proclamation to 21 July 1940.

wars.name: Estonian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Soviet attack on Narva 28 November 1918; ceasefire 3 January 1920; Treaty of Tartu 2 February 1920 on a frontier that 'corresponded roughly with the position of the front line'.
wars.note: The Estonian advance into Russia (Petseri regained by 29 March 1919, Pskov 25 May 1919) and into Latvia (Valga 31 January 1919) left no lasting territory beyond the Tartu line.

wars.name: Estonian war against the Baltische Landeswehr
wars.outcome: The war 'broke out on the southern front in Latvia on 5 June 1919'; the Estonian 3rd Division recaptured Cesis on 23 June; ceasefire on 3 July 1919 with the Estonians at the outskirts of Riga. The fighting was on Latvian soil.
wars.note: Latvia's side is in the republic-of-latvia dossier.

wars.name: Soviet ultimatum and occupation of 1940
wars.outcome: Mutual assistance treaty with Soviet bases on 28 September 1939; ultimatum of 16 June 1940; annexation as the Estonian SSR on 6 August 1940. No fighting.

certainty.note: German occupation, the Soviet invasion and the Estonian advances moved the front within the year; no treaty line yet.
The Tartu border of 2 February 1920 (frontier follows the front line); the Valga/Valka line with Latvia is not on the pages opened.

notes: Page budget 5 of 5. Cliopatria 'Estonia' 1919..1939 (4 shapes); the row 'Republic of Estonia' 1992..2024 shares Q191 and is group eu-22's republic-of-estonia: the two are one state in Estonian law (legal continuity) but this dossier ends in 1940 so that the Estonian SSR dossier (already written, predecessor estonia, successor republic-of-estonia) sits between them; the orchestrator may merge them later (the 1940-1991 interval would then be a loss and a gain, as in republic-of-latvia). The four shapes differ by 1 cell (1920) and 3 cells (1936); no page dates a border change. The Tartu page gives no border route; the war page gives only 'Setumaa and a strip east of the Narva'. Page silent: the Valga/Valka division with Latvia (1920), Ruhnu, the 1944 transfer of Petseri and the Narva east bank (a footnote of the war page; the ESSR dossier carries it), the exact day of the German arrival at Narva and Tallinn. Disagreement: Red Army entry 16 June 1940 (Baltic page) or 17 June (Estonia page). Gazetteer names needed: Setomaa. Counterparts: german-empire for the 1918 occupation (Cliopatria row 1871..1919), russian-republic for the predecessor; the Baltische Landeswehr has no dossier.
